narrative: Fire and climate dominated today's feed. A 35-year resample of lodgepole pine stands found aboveground nitrogen pools still growing after stand-replacing fire, while long-term post-fire work in a subtropical mountain region showed structural and floristic recovery decoupled. Satellite time series indicated karst vegetation shifts its phenology more strongly than non-karst areas, and a flooding experiment showed brackish water disrupting sap flux in coastal trees. On movement and landscape themes, GPS-tagged pygmy owls and a multi-taxa woodland experiment showed that connectivity and landscape context outweigh local habitat structure. Social and behavioural papers linked strong social bonds to survival in a cooperative bird, and a Science paper mapped terrestrial vertebrates at risk from sea-level rise. In methods, L-band radar mapping of tropical dry forest carbon and a machine-learning biome-boundary framework stood out alongside new R packages for camera traps and fish body size.
